2. Facts of the case in short are that the plaintiff-petitioner filed Title Suit No. 41/66 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Khulna for a declaration that the certificate case No. 595/12/C of 1948-49 and the sale held thereunder on 28.7.60 should, not be declared to have been held without jurisdiction, void and tainted with fraud and material irregularity in publishing and conducting sale. Plaintiffs case was that late Sreemonta Chatterjee died in Jaistha 1344 B.S. leaving the plaintiffs No. 1 and 2 as sons and Sarat Kumari Debi as his widow. Sree monta Chatterjee constructed a two storied building on the suit land and executed a registered deed of gift in respect of the suit property on 30.6.34 in favour of his wife Sarat Kumari Debi. Sree monta Chatterjee had several toujis and tenures with the arrears of rent were acquired by the Government under section 3(1) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act on 2.7.54 and 15.7.54 with effect from August 1954. As there were arrears of rent from the tenants to the tune of Tk. 1,00,000/- the defendant No. 4 the government started certificate case No. 595/R/C/1948-49 against the plaintiffs and their younger brother Arunendra Shekhar and mother Sarat Kumari Debi for arrears of education cess from the period of July-September 1948 amounting to Rs. 6216/- with interest and for arrears of cess of the same year amounting to Rs. 2585/- thus totaling Tk. 8,801/- and for realisation of the said Tk. 8801/- certificate sale was held on 28.7.60 and the said was purchased by defendant No. 2 for a nominal sum of Rs. 15,900/- and the said sale was confirmed on 9.11.60. 

 3. It was further case of the plaintiffs that the suit property was requisitioned by the government in requisition Case No. H.R. Misc. Cast No. 215 of 1948-49 as per East Bengal (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act, 1948 since then the Government is in possession of the same. The Government assessed the compensation at Rs. 150/- per month which was paid upto 1956 thereafter the government did not pay any compensation. The plaintiffs moved the Revenue Authority for relief but as they got no relief from there, they had to file the suit for declaration as stated above. 

 4. The auction purchaser the defendant No. 2 entered appearance and filed a written statement stating that the plaintiffs filed several applications under Order 16 rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure for production of relevant certificate case record lying with the record room of the defendant No. 1. on 7.1.74, 28.6.75, 8.9.75, 10.3.76. & 15.4.76 and the learned Subordinate Judge directed the defendant No.1 to produce the said records but the same was not complied with. It was further stated in the application that Mr. A.P. Sen, the Senior Advocate who was in charge of the case left Khulna in connection with his own personal affairs and on 13.9.76 Mr. Amjad Hossain Sardar who was his junior filed an application for time on the ground that he could not manage to engage a Senior and he was not competent to conduct the suit as there were complicated questions of law and fact involved but the learned Subordinate Judge did not grant any time and dismissed the suit for default. Thereafter the petitioner filed an application under Order 9 rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the said order of dismissal for default stating that on 12.9.76. Mr. Amjad Hossain tried to engage a senior Advocate in the suit because of the absence of Mr. Abhoy Pada Sent Senior Advocate but be could not get any Senior Advocate and himself could not prepare the case within the short period to conduct case as the case involved complicated questions of fact and law. The said application was numbered as Miscellaneous Case No. 20 of 1976. The said Misc. Case was fixed for hearing on 2.1.80 but the clerk of Mr. A. P. Sen, Senior Advocate took the date from the Court Cause List but through oversight and mistake noted in his diary 20.1.80 instead of 2.1.80 for hearing of the said Miscellaneous Case and because of the said wrong noting in the diary neither the petitioner's advocate nor the clerk of the advocate could appear on 2.1.80 for which the said Misc. Case was dismissed for default. There fatter the plaintiff-petitioners on the advice of their learned Advocate filed an application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the older of dismissal and for restoration of the same and the said application was numbered as Misc Case No. 4 of 1980. The learned Sub ordinate Judge after bearing the petitioners Advocate dismissed he same by his order dated 30.6.80 holding that the said application was not maintainable. Thereafter the petitioners fried an appeal against the said order of the learned Subordinate Judge dated 2.1.80 passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 20 of 1976 before District Judge Khulna which was numbered as Miscellaneous Appeal No. 212 of 1980. The petitioners along-with the said appeal filed an application under sections 5 and 14 of the Limitation Act for condo nation of delay in filing the appeal giving sufficient reasons. The learned District Judge admitted the appeal on 18.7.80 On 29.12.81 the appeal was heard by the Additional District Judge Court No. 1 Khulna who dismissed the same. Being aggrieved by the said order of dismissal of the appeal plaintiff-petitioners have preferred this Revisional application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the present rule.
